text:
maria: Heads-up: we're seeing a new latency spike on small-sequence requests (seq <= 16) after the kernel-selector heuristic rolled yesterday. p95 jumped ~2x in canary. baseline ~18ms -> 40-50ms. Anyone picking this up?

deploy-bot: Roll deployed: kernel-selector v2.3.7 by kai at 2319872000. Canaries enabled.

kai: that's me. thanks for flagging. do you have a simple repro or a perf flame?

maria: quick snippets from perf bench (microbench, model=redwood-7b, batch=8, seq=8):
```\nbefore (v2.3.6): p50=12ms p95=18ms p99=28ms
  profile: attn_flash_paged: 0.55, fused_flash: 0.25, enqueue/overhead: 0.20
after (v2.3.7): p50=18ms p95=45ms p99=90ms
  profile: fused_flash: 0.82, attn_flash_paged: 0.06, enqueue/overhead: 0.12
```\n
maria: Looks like selector now prefers fused_flash aggressively for short sequences which is making latency worse on our small-token common path (chat completions).

sam: interesting. did the heuristic change the cost model for kernel throughput vs latency? maybe it optimized for long sequences and ignored warm KV cache wins on paged path.

kai: the change introduced a normalized throughput estimate that factors in avg_seq * tokens_per_cycle. I may have mis-weighted the cold-KV penalty. I’ll bisect locally but need guidance on how we validated canaries.

lee: fwiw I saw KV eviction spikes in traces around the same time window — could be eviction -> repeated cold KV lookups -> fused path getting churned?

maria: here's a flame snippet from our tracing (stack-sampled):
```\n# after v2.3.7
0. fused_flash_attn.forward (dominant)
1. kv_cache.miss_handler
2. scheduler.enqueue_sync
3. device_launch_overhead
```\n
sam: hypothesis: fused_flash has worse startup latency when KV cache is cold / misaligned across contiguous requests, whereas flash_paged amortizes the KV cost better. The selector's cold-KV penalty seems undercounted.

kai: agreed. plan: bisect the selector change, run microbench with forced kernels, measure per-request KV miss rate. I can run a quick A/B: force ATTN_KERNEL=flash_paged vs ATTN_KERNEL=fused_flash on the same canary cluster.

maria: please do. I ran a quick forced run already:
```\n$ runtest --model redwood-7b --batch 8 --seq 8 --profile --force-kernel=flash_paged
p95=19ms p99=30ms
$ runtest --model redwood-7b --batch 8 --seq 8 --profile --force-kernel=fused_flash
p95=47ms p99=92ms
```\n
maria: so forcing flash_paged restores latency. This is a strong signal the selector picked a suboptimal kernel for small seqs when KV behavior isn't ideal.

sam: can you also capture KV cache occupancy histogram for these runs? need to see per-request eviction counts.

maria: attaching quick aggregated numbers (counts per 1k requests):
```\nflash_paged: avg_evictions=0.3, kv_miss_rate=2.1%
fused_flash: avg_evictions=1.8, kv_miss_rate=9.6%
```\n
lee: that lines up. fused_flash is triggering more eviction churn. maybe fused path launches more threads/cu groups that thrash L2/KV locality.

kai: I'm starting a git bisect between commits 9f3a2b..c4d8e1 (selector heuristic change). Will run microbench on each candidate and post p95. ETA ~40m.

perf-bot: Scheduled perf run: microbench redwood-7b seq=8 batch=8 (canary cluster) at 2319878000. Results will post to /perf/results/2319878000.

sam: parallel suggestion: add an override in selector config: min_seq_threshold_for_fused=32 (so fused not picked for seq<32) as a quick mitigation.

kai: good quick rollback option. I can push a config canary first (no code rollback). If that fixes, we ship config change and then debug accurate cold-KV penalty.

maria: agree. config canary is low-risk. Also we should add a regression unit test that runs microbench on seq=8/16 and asserts p95 < 30ms.

lee: I'll add a KV occupancy metric export to the observability dashboard so we can correlate evictions <> latency automatically.

kai: update: bisect round 1 (10 commits) finished: culprit narrowed to commit c1b7f2 which adjusted cold_kv_penalty factor to 0.2 -> 0.05. The cost model now undercounts cold-KV.

maria: nice find. can we patch selector to multiply cold_kv_penalty by a size-aware factor (1.0 for seq<=16)?

kai: yes. I'll prepare a quick config change: selectors.yaml: cold_kv_penalty: global* (then override for small_seq). Example:
```\ncost_model:
  cold_kv_penalty: 0.2
  overrides:
    - seq_max: 16
      cold_kv_penalty: 0.8
```\n
sam: after that we should run the same forced tests and the standard benchmark. Also run with mixed workloads (seq 8-512) to ensure no regressions for long seq.

maria: if config canary looks good, recommend ship with canary ramp and add rollback rule: if canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5 within 30m, revert config.

perf-bot: Perf run complete: /perf/results/2319878000 : forced flash_paged p95=19ms, fused_flash p95=46ms, selector-v2.3.7 p95=44ms.

kai: pushed config override to canary cluster (selector-config v2.3.7+fix). Monitoring.

maria: preliminary canary numbers look good: p95 back to ~20ms for seq<=16. No immediate impact on long-seq tail.

lee: I'll instrument some extra histograms for eviction latency and report back in 1h.

kai: follow-ups: (1) land config fix and monitor, (2) revert commit c1b7f2 or adjust cost math with better cold-KV calibration, (3) add microbench regression test in CI, (4) add dashboard correlation alert for KV eviction spikes.

maria: thanks all. great cross-team ops. Will keep this thread updated with post-mortem once we stabilize. :thumbsup:
